teamNotes.Product Designers: Use this to decide behavior, hierarchy, states, density, motion, and responsive composition.
teamNotes.Developers: Use this to identify state models, token dependencies, accessibility contracts, events, and test cases.
teamNotes.PMs: Use this to connect user goals, business rules, rollout risk, permissions, metrics, and operational ownership.
teamNotes.Content Designers: Use this to define labels, helper text, errors, empty states, success copy, and localization boundaries.
teamNotes.Researchers: Use this to track assumptions, usability risks, evidence, task success, and questions for validation.
teamNotes.Service Designers: Use this to map backstage ownership, support paths, escalation, recovery, and handoffs.
teamNotes.Design: Use this to define composition, hierarchy, affordance, state, and motion.
teamNotes.Engineering: Use this to define architecture, events, tests, data contracts, and accessibility behavior.
teamNotes.Content: Use this to define labels, error recovery, tone, and localization.
teamNotes.Research: Use this to define assumptions and validation questions.
teamNotes.Service: Use this to define support ownership and operational recovery.
teamNotes.Finance: Use this to understand spend, reconciliation, limits, exceptions, and audit evidence.
teamNotes.fallback: Use this to understand the artifact through your discipline and hand off cleanly to the next team.

rules: {{title}} must be resolved before components are selected.
The rule must be visible in human copy and in agent-readable specs.
Accessibility, content, motion, and engineering implications are part of the same decision.
decisionTree: What user state or product risk activates {{title}}?
Which semantic primitive expresses that decision?
Which component or pattern consumes it?
What should fail if the decision is missing?

tokenModel.copy: Public API is semantic. Raw hex, pixel, bezier, duration, and implementation values stay private behind platform adapters.

must: Trace Foundation -> Primitive -> Component -> Pattern -> Template before implementation
Define success, loading, empty, error, disabled, permission, offline, and recovery states
Preserve accessibility under keyboard, touch, screen reader, high contrast, and reduced motion
Keep human documentation and machine specification synchronized
rejectIf: map system lacks permission and fallback states

foundation.overviewCopy: {{title}} is not a styling preference. It is a decision layer that shapes component behavior, pattern rules, template structure, and agent output before UI is assembled.
foundation.roleGridCopy: Like the reference foundation template, each foundation needs visible role groups. These groups make the rule teachable, reusable, and testable.
foundation.architectureCopy: {{title}} follows the same inheritance chain across design, code, and agents.
foundation.visualExplanationCopy: The visual is schematic but specific: it shows how {{title}} changes hierarchy, rhythm, recovery, or state instead of decorating a card.
contractRows: What product condition activates the foundation.
Using visual style without product rationale.
Accessibility, content, motion, and engineering gates.
Agent output that looks plausible but violates system rules.

Tone: Calm base state for ordinary work.

primitive.overviewCopy: Primitives are implementation-facing contracts. They prevent teams and agents from reaching for raw CSS, raw values, or one-off component behavior.
primitive.demoCopy: This mirrors the reference primitive template: show the primitive doing one job with clear labels, semantic roles, and token names.
responsibilities: Render {{title}} through semantic roles instead of raw implementation values.
Expose a small API that maps to foundations and token aliases.
Work across density, responsive breakpoints, keyboard, touch, screen reader, high contrast, and reduced motion when relevant.
Provide a clear prevents statement so teams know what not to do.
primitive.tokenChainCopy: Design System's reference model uses ref -> sys -> comp. We keep that idea while preserving our naming conventions.
apiRows: Semantic role consumed by components and agents.
Only expose states that the primitive owns.
Maps to Frame and Energy behavior.
No raw values in public API.
usageRules: Use {{title}} when the product needs a stable concept shared by design, engineering, and agents.
Do not expose raw implementation values as public API.
Every example must include success, empty, loading, error, disabled, permission, and offline behavior when relevant.
anatomy: Container: owns layout, density, focus boundary, and responsive behavior.
Content: labels, values, helper text, icons, and metadata.
Controls: primary action, secondary action, overflow, and escape.
State layer: loading, invalid, disabled, permission-blocked, offline, optimistic, and error.
states: Default, hover, active, focus, selected, expanded, collapsed.
Loading, stale, syncing, optimistic, empty, invalid, error.
Reduced motion, high contrast, keyboard-only, and touch-only.
accessibility: {{title}} must define name, role, state, focus order, and escape behavior.
No meaning may depend only on color, position, pointer hover, speed, or memory.
Motion must respect reduced motion while preserving the information carried by movement.
Touch targets, keyboard routes, screen reader copy, contrast, and recovery paths are required.

density.coordinatorCopy: Density is not a component size switch. It is the surface-level scale contract that coordinates related primitives before components render.
dependencies: Gaps, panel padding, page rhythm, inline spacing.
Text role scale and label rhythm for the active context.
Icon size and optical balance with labels and targets.
Ring offset and minimum visible focus area across densities.
Spinner, skeleton, and progress rhythm at the active density.
Readable unavailable state and reason density.
Viewport thresholds that choose the surface density.
density.decisionCopy: Density responds to viewport and product context. Components inherit it; they do not expose independent public size controls.
decisionRows: Fleet manager tables, filters, comparison views, repeated desktop actions.
Efficient rhythm with readable type, clear grouping, and protected targets.
Forms, documentation, configuration, most desktop and laptop processs.
Balanced scanning, comfortable labels, normal rhythm.
Driver mobile, phablets, high-focus review, TV/wallboard-like dashboards.
More generous spacing, stronger hierarchy, larger controls, and distance-friendly reading.

fallbackQuestions: Can users explain what {{title}} lets them do without facilitator help?
Where does trust increase or collapse?
Which terms are misunderstood by drivers, fleet managers, admins, or finance users?
What failure mode creates the highest support burden?

pattern.fallbackPurpose: Patterns are no longer just journeys. Each pattern declares entry conditions, system decisions, failure modes, components, metrics, and research questions.
fallbackDecisions: What condition brings the user into {{title}}?
What data, permission, device, location, or role gates the system?
What is the safest next action and what evidence supports it?
What happens when data is missing, stale, denied, offline, or risky?
fallbackFailureModes: {{title}} must define loading, empty, error, permission denied, offline, and stale-data behavior.
Every blocking state needs owner, recovery copy, and support or retry path.
Mobile patterns must include touch and reduced-motion alternatives.
Desktop patterns must include keyboard, density, table, filter, export, and audit behavior when relevant.
fallbackContractRows: Loading, empty, error, denied, offline, stale.

fallbackItems: Expose semantic props, events, and states. Do not expose raw token values.
Use Edenred Black only for display/title/numeral roles and Ubuntu for the rest.
Use Material Symbols through the Symbol foundation, not as arbitrary glyphs.
Use Motion for UI transitions, dotLottie for illustrative animation, and ECharts for dashboard charts.
Define tests for keyboard, screen reader naming, reduced motion, loading, error, offline, permission, and localization.

qualityGates: No raw values outside reference tokens.
Demo, states, responsive behavior, accessibility, and agent spec must stay in sync.
Examples must include a real user job, not a decorative placeholder.
componentProps: State must change copy and accessibility.
Rendered with fallback if icon font is unavailable.
patternProps: Chosen by context before selecting components.
What the system chooses and why.
Denied, error, offline, and support paths.
defaultProps: Public API uses semantic roles only.

do: Show concrete user context and operational consequence.
Document responsive behavior for laptop, tablet, and mobile.
Connect the artifact to tokens, patterns, and quality gates.
doNot: Use decorative examples that do not teach behavior.
Depend on icon fonts without a visible fallback.
Reuse one template structure when the product job is different.

demoMatrix.copy: Every component should expose state, density, and platform combinations. Scale belongs to Density, not public component size.

brief: Improve {{title}} using the current Design System layer contract.
Include the product context, states, accessibility, reusable output, and tests.
Ask before changing foundations, primitives, patterns, or template behavior.
canDecide: Choose examples that make the product job concrete.
Fill missing state, accessibility, and recovery details from the component contract.
Suggest wording or reusable documentation improvements that reduce future work.
mustAsk: Changing foundations, primitives, tokens, or visual language rules.
Creating new patterns, product flows, permissions, analytics, or service behavior.
Copying behavior from the ZIP instead of translating it through Design System.
preserve: The current tab structure and section names.
Design System foundations and primitives as source of truth.
Accessibility, state coverage, responsive behavior, and tests.
Reusable output that strengthens the next component, not only this page.

copy.foundation: The example shows how the foundation changes product behavior, copy, hierarchy, and recovery, not only visual decoration.
copy.primitive: The example shows the public semantic token contract and how it appears in a driver or fleet manager interface.
copy.component: The example shows a realistic state with labels, data, actions, and failure or accessibility implications.
copy.pattern: The example shows the user journey, key screens, decisions, and recovery paths for the pattern.
copy.template: The example shows the template as a complete product surface with navigation, primary work area, and operational state.
copy.fallback: A concrete example tied to product work.

Tone: Direct, calm, no jokes. Explain what is safe and what to do next.
Try another payment method or call fleet support.
Voice: Short repair copy with a clear resend action.
Your code expired. Request a new one.
Frame: Place urgent exceptions above trend exploration.
7 vehicles need attention before spend analysis.
Energy: Quiet base state; only urgent anomalies pulse once.
Motion: Sheet rises from selected station pin to preserve spatial continuity.
Reduced motion uses instant reveal plus focus move.
Accessibility: Nearby stations must also exist as a list with distance and route action.
Location denied never blocks station search.
fallback: {{title}} changes what the interface emphasizes, says, or prevents.
The rule is visible to humans and agents.

Permission Matrix: Drivers: edit - Vehicles: edit - Finance: read
fallback: Ready, loading, error, disabled and permission states.

componentChecklist: Includes success, loading, empty, error, disabled and permission-blocked states.
Uses Material Symbol {{icon}} with accessible naming.
Defines keyboard, touch, reduced-motion and screen reader behavior.

journeyCopy.Entry: The user arrives with a concrete job: {{summary}}
journeyCopy.Orient: The interface explains current state, available actions, constraints, and risks.
journeyCopy.Act: The user performs the primary action with clear affordances and safe defaults.
journeyCopy.Confirm: The system confirms outcome, next step, and any operational consequence.
journeyCopy.Recover: Errors, denied permissions, offline states, and support paths remain explicit.

fallback: Recovery rate after error, denied permission, timeout, or offline state.
Operational reduction in escalations, manual corrections, or repeated work.

accessibility.statePrecedenceFallback: State precedence must be explicit and stable.

stackPage.title: Libraries are governed primitives.
stackPage.copy: The stack is intentionally small: Motion for UI behavior, dotLottie for illustrative states, Material Symbols for iconography, ECharts for dashboards, maps for station discovery, and Edenred plus Ubuntu for typography.
